name: Illusion of Asymmetric Insight
description: People tend to believe they understand other people better than those people understand them. We treat our own inner life as richly diagnostic while reading other people from their outward behavior with more confidence than they deserve.
design_relevance_note: Relevant to user research, stakeholder alignment, and teamwork: teams can overestimate how well they 'get' users or colleagues while underestimating how opaque they themselves remain, creating false confidence in empathy and consensus.
prevalence_note: Known in social psychology and occasionally cited in polarization or team-conflict writing, but rarely named as a standard day-to-day design heuristic.

findings.description: Across studies, people judged their knowledge of peers or groups to exceed those others' knowledge of them, and the paper traced this asymmetry partly to giving one's own private thoughts more diagnostic weight than other people's observable behavior.
findings.source_title: You don't know me, but I know you: The illusion of asymmetric insight.
findings.source_venue: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology
